answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a falcon as the anchor of the cost.
